text: Let love for one another continue.
Do not neglect hospitality, for by it some have entertained angels without knowing it.
Remember those in prison as if you were bound with them, and those who are mistreated, since you yourselves are in the body as well.
Marriage is to be honored by all, and the marriage bed kept undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
Keep your life free from the love of money, and be content with what you have, for he himself has said, "I will never leave you nor forsake you."
So we can say with confidence, "The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can anyone do to me?"
Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you. Consider how their lives turned out, and imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange, unfamiliar teachings. It is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by rules about food, which have never benefited those who follow them.

versions.text: Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange teachings. It is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by food regulations, which have never benefited those who follow them.
versions.explanation: The Greek has two adjectives, "varied" and "strange/foreign"; the current rendering collapses them. Also "food regulations" is a slightly technical phrase for oral reading; "rules about food" flows more naturally.

text: We have an altar from which those who serve at the tabernacle have no right to eat.
For the high priest carries the blood of the animals into the sanctuary as a sin offering, but their bodies are burned outside the camp.

versions.text: For the bodies of those animals whose blood the high priest brings into the sanctuary as a sin offering are burned outside the camp.
versions.explanation: The current sentence separates the subject ("the bodies") from its verb ("are burned") by a long relative clause, which is hard to follow when read aloud. Splitting the clause preserves the sense while giving a clearer oral rhythm.

text: And so Jesus also suffered outside the gate, to make the people holy through his own blood.
Let us then go out to him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace he bore.
For here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the one that is to come.
So then, through him let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise—the fruit of lips that confess his name.
And do not neglect to do good and to share with others, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.

Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they keep watch over your souls as those who must give an account. Do this so that their work may be a joy and not a burden, for that would be of no advantage to you.

versions.text: Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they keep watch over your souls as those who must give an account. Let them do this with joy and not with groaning, for that would be of no advantage to you.
versions.explanation: The Greek ἵνα-clause states the purpose of the readers' obedience, not a separate command directed at the leaders. Recasting it as a purpose clause keeps the logical link intact.

text: Pray for us. We are convinced that we have a clear conscience, desiring to live honorably in every way.
And I urge you all the more to pray, so that I may be restored to you soon.
Now may the God of peace, who brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of the eternal covenant,
equip you with everything good to do his will, working in us what is pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever. Amen.
I urge you, brothers and sisters, bear with this word of encouragement, for I have written to you only briefly.
You should know that our brother Timothy has been released. If he comes soon, I will bring him with me when I see you.
Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send you greetings.
Grace be with you all.
